source.title_on_document: AI as an element to overcome creative fixation in design teams

paper_design_summary: A facilitated exploratory workshop involved 19 architecture and industrial-design students in 8 teams developing concepts to minimize domestic garbage (PDF p. 3, printed p. 411, sections 3.1 and 3.3). Teams were randomly assigned different LLM and text-to-image tools for research, concept creation and visualization, with all teams using AI (PDF pp. 3-4, printed pp. 411-412, section 3.3 and Table 1). Two design experts evaluated final concepts using the Consensual Assessment Technique, but the results provide qualitative judgments without numerical scores or between-model contrasts (PDF p. 4, printed p. 412, section 4).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Particular AI tools were randomly assigned to teams for the workshop phases, regardless of design discipline; the resulting LLM/text-to-image combinations are listed in Table 1. This is team-level random assignment of AI configurations within a supervised exploratory workshop. The method of forming teams is not stated; all teams followed the same phase sequence.
assignment.quote: Each group was assigned a particular AI in each phase in a random manner, regardless of the discipline (designers and architects).
assignment.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 412), section 3.3 Design task, opening paragraph and Table 1; phase sequence on PDF p. 3 (printed p. 411).

participants.who: Architecture bachelor’s and industrial-design master’s students recruited by open invitation at the Architecture Faculty. The reported workshop sample is 19 students in 8 teams (5 teams of 2 members and 3 teams of 3 members); every team presented a final concept and the results were evaluated. The paper does not give a separate randomized count or separate analysis sample, and does not link team sizes to named teams or AI configurations.
participants.quote: A total of 19 students (11 male and 8 female) participated, with ages ranging from 19 to 38.
participants.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 411), section 3.1 Participants and section 3.3 Design task; evaluation of team outputs on PDF p. 4 (printed p. 412), section 4 Results.

ai_tool.name_model: LLMs: ChatGPT, Claude.AI, Gemini. Text-to-image tools: Krea.AI, Vizcom, Meta, Leonardo.AI, Dall-E3, Adobe Firefly. Further model versions are not stated.
ai_tool.how_used: Teams prompted assigned LLMs during research, used LLMs and text-to-image tools during concept creation, and concentrated on detailed concept visuals during concept development. LLM-generated image descriptions were copied into image generators. Some teams switched tools when frustrated with results. PDF pp. 3-4 (printed pp. 411-412), section 3.3 and section 4; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 414), section 4.

task.description: Teams framed a problem, generated and developed concepts, and presented a final concept with images in response to how to minimize garbage production in a domestic environment. PDF pp. 3-4 (printed pp. 411-412), sections 3.3 and 4.
task.duration: Two-hour workshop; research, concept creation and concept development each lasted 20 minutes; final presentations were allocated 5 minutes per team. PDF p. 3 (printed p. 411), sections 3.1 and 3.3.

outcomes.name: Overall creativity of final design concepts (Consensual Assessment Technique)
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Across the AI-assisted teams, two design experts evaluated overall creativity using CAT, considering problem framing, similarity to existing ideas and context specificity. The authors describe the design solutions as obvious and generic, with inadequate specificity to the local context. No numerical creativity scores, arm-specific results or statistical contrast between AI configurations are reported; this entry records the qualitative main result.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 412), section 4 Results, paragraph beginning The results were evaluated for overall creativity.

eligibility.reason: The text explicitly states random assignment of AI tools to teams, providing randomized variation in AI configurations (PDF p. 4, printed p. 412, section 3.3 and Table 1). Only 19 students participated across 8 teams, below the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 3, printed p. 411, sections 3.1 and 3.3), so core is no. Two experts evaluated the final design outputs for overall creativity using CAT (PDF p. 4, printed p. 412, section 4), although no numerical scores or between-configuration contrasts are printed. Under the codebook, randomized studies below 50 people belong in the screening report and have no context classification.

one_line_finding: Among 19 students in 8 teams assigned AI tools at random, two design experts evaluated final concepts as obvious and generic; no numerical creativity scores or between-model contrasts were reported (PDF pp. 3-4, printed pp. 411-412, sections 3.1, 3.3 and 4).
